item.title: Pomegranate Extract
item.description:
What it is: Pomegranate extract from Punica granatum fruit is rich in punicalagins and anthocyanins that support cardiovascular health, reduce inflammation, and provide potent antioxidant protection.

Benefits

Cardiovascular Health

  • Reduces blood pressure (5-8 mmHg typical)
  • Improves endothelial function and blood flow
  • Reduces arterial plaque formation
  • Supports cholesterol profiles
  • Anti-inflammatory in cardiovascular system

Antioxidant Protection

  • Punicalagins among most potent antioxidants known
  • Protects against LDL oxidation
  • Protects cellular DNA
  • Supports mitochondrial health
  • Anti-aging antioxidant support

Anti-Inflammatory

  • Reduces TNF-alpha and IL-6
  • Systemic inflammation reduction
  • Supports joint health

Sexual Function Support

  • Improves blood flow to tissues
  • May improve erectile function
  • Improved nitric oxide and endothelial function

Dosage

Cardiovascular: 250-500 mg daily Enhanced: 500-750 mg daily Full: 750-1,000 mg daily Timing: With meals containing fat Duration: 4-8 weeks cardiovascular; 8+ weeks antioxidant benefits

item.title: Fisetin
item.description:
What it is: Fisetin is a plant flavonoid with senolytic properties—meaning it can selectively eliminate senescent (aged, dysfunctional) cells that accumulate with age. Emerging longevity research suggests senolytics may reverse aging processes at the cellular level, offering potential rejuvenation beyond conventional anti-aging approaches.

What Is Fisetin?

Fisetin is a naturally occurring flavonoid found in strawberries, apples, cucumbers, onions, and other plant foods. While it can be obtained from diet (one strawberry contains ~0.2 mg fisetin), therapeutic doses (100-500 mg) require supplementation.

item.title: Ginger
item.description:
What it is: Ginger is a potent anti-inflammatory root used for thousands of years to soothe digestion, reduce nausea, and support joint health. Modern research confirms its traditional use—supplemental ginger reduces nausea, joint pain, and inflammation with effects comparable to some medications but without side effects.

What Is Ginger?

Ginger (Zingiber officinale) is a rhizome (underground stem) of a tropical plant, with a spicy, warming flavor profile. Used in traditional medicine for over 2,500 years—particularly in Chinese, Indian, and Southeast Asian traditions—ginger is one of the few herbal remedies with substantial modern clinical validation.

item.title: Tart Cherry
item.description:
What it is: Tart cherry is a fruit extract rich in anthocyanins—powerful antioxidants and anti-inflammatory compounds that improve sleep quality, reduce muscle soreness, and support recovery. Clinical research shows it works comparably to some sleep medications without side effects, making it one of the most evidence-backed natural sleep aids available.

What Is Tart Cherry?

Tart cherry (Prunus cerasus) is a sour cherry variety grown primarily in North America, distinct from sweet cherries commonly eaten fresh. While tart cherries are too sour for fresh consumption, they’re ideal for juices, concentrates, and supplements—forms that concentrate their bioactive compounds.

item.title: Krill Oil
item.description:
What Is Krill Oil?

Krill oil is derived from Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba), small crustaceans approximately 1-2 cm in length that form the foundation of the Southern Ocean food chain. Krill oil is fundamentally different from conventional fish oil due to its unique lipid structure and intrinsic antioxidant content.

Biological Source:

  • Primary habitat: Antarctic waters, deepest and most pristine marine environment on Earth
  • Biomass: Estimated 500+ million tonnes; most abundant animal biomass on Earth (sustainable harvesting)
  • Natural function: Krill store lipids as energy reserves for Antarctic ecosystem, particularly for whales, penguins, and seals
  • Sustainability: Krill species are fast-reproducing, cold-water adapted; harvesting represents <1% of total biomass; certified by Marine Stewardship Council (MSC)

Unique Lipid Composition: Unlike fish oil (triglyceride-based), krill oil contains naturally occurring phospholipid-bound omega-3 fatty acids (approximately 40-50% of total lipids), which fundamentally alters bioavailability and mechanism of action.
